formula: price(inv) = base + sign * amp * f(|inv - I0|); floored at price_floor and rounded to nearest dollar
T_definition: Production capacity of one 5x5 field over a 24-day window at optimal watering with no fertilizer. Animal T is pre-discounted 30% for wheat-feed overhead and one build day. Calibration horizon, not the 30-day season.
target_definition: Moving T units past I0 shifts price by target * base.

shape_functions.hinge: u = x / T; f(x) = u + 8 * max(0, u - 1)^2. Linear below T, quadratic spike above T. f(T) = 1 by construction.

trading_rules.seeds_and_animals: Unlimited supply at fixed prices. Not on this curve.
trading_rules.roundtrip_identity: Immediate buy then sell of the same item against an unchanged market nets exactly zero.
trading_rules.concurrent_orders: Orders process one unit at a time across both players. Same-turn opponent dumps move your price.
trading_rules.floor_behavior: At $1 the unit is still bought but is not added to market inventory, so the floor stays responsive to later buys.
trading_rules.money_stop: If a player runs out of money mid-order, the remaining units are dropped.

inventory_drains.town_center: 1 of every product except fertilizer every 24 turns (once per day, flat all season).
inventory_drains.shops: Each unlocked shop instance consumes 1 of every demanded product every 4 turns. Single-product shops consume 2x. Up to 8 instances, drawn with replacement every 3 days.

WHEAT.behavior: Panics on scarcity, absorbs gluts. Safe to overproduce.

CARROT.behavior: Calm near base until demand passes T, then scarcity spikes. Glut falls to $1 by I0+2T. Consumed by pet cafes (2x) and farmers markets.

TOMATO.behavior: Hinge scarcity. Smaller T than carrot, so gluts hit sooner. Consumed by pizza shops and farmers markets.

STRAWBERRY.behavior: Premium. Modest glut drives price to $1. Time and bundle sales.

MELON.behavior: Barely reacts to scarcity, crashes hard on overproduction. Opposite of wheat.

EGG.behavior: Hinge scarcity, wheat-like glut absorption. Produced by geese. Consumed by bakeries and brunch spots.

MILK.behavior: Premium. Small T; overproduction hits the floor quickly. Produced by cows.

WOOL.behavior: Melon-like crash at smaller scale. Produced by sheep. Yarn stores consume 2x.

FERTILIZER.behavior: Symmetric linear. Buyable and sellable. Town center does not consume it.

premium_rule: base > 100 and above_target > 1: even modest gluts go to the $1 floor.
